newsitem.title: USA: Forcenergy ups debt issue by $25 mln.
newsitem.headline: Forcenergy ups debt issue by $25 mln.

text.p: Forcenergy Inc on Tuesday said it increased the size of its high-yield debt offering to fund an anticipated difference between cash flow and its 1997 capital budget.

The issue, priced on Tuesday through lead manager Salomon Brothers, was upped by $25 million to $200 million and priced with an 8-1/2 percent coupon to yield 8.60 percent, said J. Russell Porter, vice president in corporate development.
Strong investor demand allowed the adjustment, he said.
Forcenergy in January said it planned to spend about $195 million on 1997 capital projects excluding acquisitions, which would be pursued opportunistically throughout the year.
Other proceeds from Tuesday's sale will be used to repay all outstanding loans under its credit facility.
The entire deal puts Forcenergy in a better position to execute its acquisition strategy, Porter said. Last year, Forcenergy spent nearly $150 million on acquisitions.
"After this deal we've got a senior credit faciliy of $195 million with nothing drawn on it," he said. "We could probably add to that by $50 million to $75 million if we desire to."

A higher credit facility would not affect the company's credit ratings, he said. The company's senior subordinated debt is currently rated B1 by Moody's Investors Service Inc and B-plus by Standard & Poor's.
Forcenergy is an independent oil and gas company engaged in the development, exploration, acquisition and production of domestic oil and natural gas properties.
